title: PlantVillage Nuru identifies cassava disease symptoms at 65% accuracy against 40–58% for extension agents
summary: In a field evaluation in Kenya and Tanzania, the offline PlantVillage Nuru app identified cassava disease symptoms with 65% accuracy, above extension agents (40–58%) and farmers (18–31%).
account: Nuru is a deep-learning object-detection model inside the free PlantVillage Android app, trained on 2,756 cassava leaf images and able to run offline. PlantVillage at Pennsylvania State University developed it with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center and others. Researchers at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture compared Nuru with cassava experts, agricultural extension officers and farmers. The targets were cassava mosaic disease, cassava brown streak disease and cassava green mite damage. They inspected plants in the field and scored a 170-image cassava symptom recognition assessment tool built from a farm in Mkuranga, Tanzania. The assessment tool was also used with 30 extension agents and 50 farmers from Busia County, western Kenya, before and after they were introduced to the app. The 2020 test used Nuru V2.6.0-39, released in June 2020. Nuru diagnosed cassava disease symptoms at 65% accuracy in 2020 versus 40–58% for extension agents and 18–31% for farmers. It rose to 74–88% with six leaves per plant assessed. Mild symptoms were recognized at only 13–37%. Extension officers showed no significant gain in accuracy after two weeks of using the app (49.9% to 50.5%). No farm-level outcome is reported. In September 2024, staff of WAVE, the center that spread the app in Côte d'Ivoire, reported on 146 surveyed users in three departments. They reported that 45% kept using the app after the project ended and that 56% had stopped.

display.answer: The makers' evaluation in Frontiers in Plant Science of 18 December 2020 supplies the accuracy figures, including 65% in 2020 and 74–88% with six leaves per plant. WAVE staff wrote the September 2024 study in Frontiers in Agronomy on the app's adoption in Côte d'Ivoire.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: In a field evaluation in Kenya and Tanzania, the offline PlantVillage Nuru app identified cassava disease symptoms with 65% accuracy, above extension agents (40–58%) and farmers (18–31%).
fields.account: Nuru is a deep-learning object-detection model inside the free PlantVillage Android app, trained on 2,756 cassava leaf images and able to run offline. PlantVillage at Pennsylvania State University developed it with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center and others. Researchers at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture compared Nuru with cassava experts, agricultural extension officers and farmers. The targets were cassava mosaic disease, cassava brown streak disease and cassava green mite damage. They inspected plants in the field and scored a 170-image cassava symptom recognition assessment tool built from a farm in Mkuranga, Tanzania. The assessment tool was also used with 30 extension agents and 50 farmers from Busia County, western Kenya, before and after they were introduced to the app. The 2020 test used Nuru V2.6.0-39, released in June 2020. Nuru diagnosed cassava disease symptoms at 65% accuracy in 2020 versus 40–58% for extension agents and 18–31% for farmers. It rose to 74–88% with six leaves per plant assessed. Mild symptoms were recognized at only 13–37%. Extension officers showed no significant gain in accuracy after two weeks of using the app (49.9% to 50.5%). No farm-level outcome is reported. In September 2024, staff of WAVE, the center that spread the app in Côte d'Ivoire, reported on 146 surveyed users in three departments. They reported that 45% kept using the app after the project ended and that 56% had stopped.
